findings.resolution: Fixed by the StringVar(master=root) repair and regeneration; both figures now display 'Победил игрок X!' / 'Победил игрок O!' alongside the green highlight, so the claim is now demonstrated rather than contradicted.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Defines the game's colour palette, justifies the deliberate use of classic tk.Button for cells rather than ttk, and insists that colour must not be the only signal of a win.

X is #5B24F9 and O is #DB2777, applied via fg= on tk.Button, with a neutral fallback for an empty cell. -- confirmed -- notebook 17-22 reads back btn.cget('fg') as '#5B24F9' then '#DB2777'; tic_tac_toe.py declares the same MARK_COLOR mapping and applies it with the '#0D0230' fallback.

tk.Button is chosen because direct fg=/bg= colouring is simple and predictable, whereas a ttk theme usually overrides per-widget colouring set that way. -- confirmed -- ttk widget appearance is theme-controlled via ttk.Style rather than per-widget fg/bg options, so the stated reason is technically correct and the choice genuinely justified rather than an oversight. Consistent with chapter 16.12, which the lesson explicitly acknowledges departing from.

The winner is visible by more than colour: the X/O letters remain and the status explicitly says 'Победил игрок X!'. -- REFUTED AS SHIPPED, now true -- the code does set that status (verified: status_var == 'Победил игрок X!'), but as found x-win.png and o-win.png rendered no status at all, so the green highlight WAS the only signal. After the F-001 fix the figures show the status text and the accessibility claim holds.

After the game ends the marks become muted because the widget is disabled. -- confirmed -- render() sets state='disabled' when game_over, and the disabled Button draws its text in disabledforeground, visible in the captures as grey X/O.
